title: HAL: Accurate, Private, and Efficient Sample Alignment for Multimodal Federated Learning

problem.claim: VMFL must align multimodal samples held by different clients for collaborative training.

gap.claim: Existing methods assume cross-client sample alignment, but independently collected data often lacks shared identifiers, so the assumption rarely holds in practice.

contributions.claim: HAL is a hashing-based VMFL framework that operates without pre-aligned samples.
HAL combines privacy-preserving cross-modal sample identification using LSH, shift-orthogonal hashing, and secure Hamming distance estimation with a neighbor-aware cross-attention fusion strategy.
The authors establish that shift-orthogonal hashing reduces distance-estimation errors and that secure Hamming distance estimation satisfies differential privacy.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report proving reduced distance-estimation errors for shift-orthogonal hashing and differential privacy for secure Hamming distance estimation.
On two real-world datasets, the authors report that HAL improves cross-modal retrieval accuracy by over 63% against five SOTA baselines.
The authors report achieving up to 154× speedup against five SOTA baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: VMFL enables clients with different modalities to train models collaboratively.
Existing approaches rely on aligned samples, an assumption that commonly fails when data is collected independently without shared identifiers.
HAL addresses unaligned data through privacy-preserving sample identification based on hashing and neighbor-aware cross-attention fusion.
The authors report theoretical privacy and error guarantees and improvements in retrieval accuracy and speed on two real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: Efficient similarity retrieval, modality-gap handling, secure distance estimation, and fusion are treated as separate components of the alignment pipeline.

interpretation.claim: A multimodal federated-learning system may benefit from decomposing alignment into retrieval, privacy, and downstream fusion responsibilities.

application.claim: Use a staged alignment design when multimodal clients lack shared identifiers and downstream modeling can consume aligned-neighbor signals.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this decomposition is suitable for settings with pre-aligned samples, modalities beyond text and image, or requirements different from the reported datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the two real-world datasets.
The abstract does not provide experimental settings, metric definitions, or statistical details.
The abstract does not specify differential-privacy parameters or the full security model.
The abstract does not describe limitations, failure cases, or computational and communication costs beyond the reported speedup.
